title.narrative: Beneficiaries that receive support under the smart device financing scheme

comment.narrative:
The call for proposals for the subsidy window under the Device Access Fund (DAF) closed in early April, 2025. RISA and BRD aim to onboard selected providers by the end of June 2025. Registration of eligible beneficiaries will be undertaken in parallel, targeting the same timeline. This would enable distributions of subsidized smart devices to begin in July 2025 to at least 100,000 beneficiaries.
This target will be revised downwards to reflect this in the upcoming restructuring, also reflecting the budget cut to this activity.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries that receive support under the smart device financing scheme

A forthcoming restructuring is expected to reduce the funding allocation for the Fund, and thus the target set will be revised downwards.

title.narrative: Digital startups supported creating and/or leveraging a digital technology solution

comment.narrative:
A handful of digital start-ups have been supported at industry/fundraising events, and several start-ups are now being supported by ecosystem support organization (ESO) that are receiving project funding for capability enhancement through technology upgrades and training.
More start-ups are due to be supported as further grants are being awarded to more ESOs and the selection for direct early-stage financing grants for start-ups is being finalized. Participation of several start-ups at industry/fundraising events is also planned in the next few months.
This indicator will be revised downwards in the upcoming restructuring to reflect funding cuts to linked activities.

Progress is expected very soon, as grants are set to awarded to ecosystem support organization that aid digital start-ups; and grants to digital start-ups will be awarded under the early-stage financing mechanism by Q1 2025 at the latest.

Results will only be registered following the launch of further activities under sub-component 3.1, including the early stage financing facility and improved ecosystem support services for digital start-ups. At least 11 start-up are due to benefit from attending an overseas industry investor conference in October 2023.

This indicator will be revised to focus solely on start-up directly receiving financial assistance in the planned restructuring, reducing the target to 40 based on a budget cut to this activity.
Hanga Venture Ignite was launched in February 2025. 259 start-ups applied, and selection of at least 30 start-ups is being finalized that will receive early-stage financing.

title.narrative: Digital startups supported creating and/or leveraging a digital technology solution

comment.narrative: A handful of digital start-ups have been supported at industry events. title.narrative: Graduates from specialized digital skills training employed or in education within 12 months after completion

comment.narrative: Rwanda Coding Academy (RCA) has doubled its annual enrolment of students from 60 to 120, thanks to the support being provided by the project. However, as training is ongoing no results can yet be reported.
Between January – June 2023, an initial batch of 136,528 people have been trained in digital literacy under the Digital Ambassadors Program.

title.narrative: Additional internet access points established (connected govt. offices, schools, hospital and marketplaces etc.)

comment.narrative: RISA is due to connect 374 schools in rural areas outside of Kigali by December 2023.  Recent acquisition of additional bandwidth capacity for Rwanda’s research and educational network will also allow 63 higher education institutions to be connected to improved broadband services. Government is still finalizing the site selection and plans for connecting the remaining 2,100+ sites required to reach the target in full.

title.narrative: Public sector officials trained in digital skills

comment.narrative: 20 public sector officials from across government have undertaken CISSP certificate cybersecurity training through the AfricaFIRST program, funded under the project. A further 57 IT officials began training in the reporting period January – June 2023.
